entities.name: PHA4GE bioinformatics infrastructure resources
entities.description: Living repository of PHA4GE-developed guidance and resources on bioinformatics infrastructure for public-health genomics. Use its individual documents to frame local requirements; it is not a hardware purchasing specification.

entities.name: Implementing pathogen genomics: a Public Health England case study
entities.description: Case study of establishing a central WGS service and moving a national bacteriology reference laboratory to genomics-led workflows, including surveillance and outbreak investigation. Describes a 2018 implementation rather than a current procurement template.

entities.name: APHL Next Generation Sequencing Implementation Guide
entities.description: Public-health laboratory guide to planning NGS implementation, including facilities, workforce, workflows and programme needs. Published in 2016; equipment examples and costs should not be treated as current.

entities.name: ECDC expert opinion on WGS for public-health surveillance
entities.description: 2016 assessment of WGS-based typing, inter-laboratory comparability, bioinformatics harmonisation and integration with epidemiological surveillance in Europe. Useful for programme history and design questions, not as current technical guidance.

sources.name: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control

entities.name: ECDC expert opinion on next-generation typing for food- and waterborne diseases
entities.description: 2015 country-level implementation guide covering sampling, sequencing, analysis, storage and interagency collaboration for Salmonella, Listeria, VTEC and Campylobacter surveillance. Its technical assumptions require current local review.

sources.name: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control

entities.name: Public health implementation of pathogen genomics: accreditation and ISO standards
entities.description: Ballard and colleagues explain quality systems, test validation and accreditation considerations when moving pathogen genomics into public-health practice.

entities.name: Accelerating bioinformatics implementation in public health
entities.description: Libuit and colleagues describe one operational approach to reproducible, auditable and scalable pathogen-genomics analysis in public-health laboratories, using open workflows and a cloud analysis platform. It is an example, not a vendor-neutral prescription.

entities.name: UKHSA Pathogen Genomics Strategy
entities.description: UK public-health strategy for accredited and resilient pathogen-genomics services, shared infrastructure, workforce, governance and public-health impact. A national example, not a universal implementation standard.

entities.name: Australian National Microbial Genomics Framework for Public Health 2025–2027
entities.description: National strategic framework and implementation activities for integrating microbial genomics into Australia's public-health system.

relationships.subject: https://github.com/pha4ge/infrastructure-resources
relationships.description: The repository identifies the PHA4GE Infrastructure Working Group as the place to join further discussion.

relationships.subject: https://doi.org/10.1099/mgen.0.001097
relationships.description: The paper discusses ISO 15189 as a medical-laboratory standard relevant to pathogen-genomics accreditation.

evidence.locator: International Organization for Standardization: two key laboratory standards

relationships.description: The paper discusses ISO 17025 for testing laboratories alongside ISO 15189 for medical laboratories.
